# Xenobiology
Xenobiology is the branch of Science that breeds [bold]slimes[/bold], mutates them into new colours, and renders them down into [bold]extracts[/bold]. Extracts are worth research points, sell to Cargo for Federal Bills, and react with chemicals to make useful items and potions.
## Getting started
- Research [color=#a4885c]Basic Xenobiology[/color] (Experimental, tier 1). It unlocks the [bold]slime scanner[/bold] and the boards for the [bold]xenobiology console[/bold] and the [bold]slime processor[/bold]. - Order a [bold]gray slime crate[/bold] from [color=orange]Cargo[/color] (Science category). Two gray slimes are enough to start a whole lab. - Order [bold]monkey cubes[/bold] from Cargo (Livestock). Slimes eat monkeys. - Build a pen with windows or grilles so the slimes stay put, and put the console where it can see the pen.
## Breeding - Slimes eat any monkey within a few tiles. Each bite feeds the slime. - A well-fed slime [bold]splits[/bold]. Each child has a chance to [bold]mutate[/bold] into a new colour instead of copying its parent. - Feed the console monkey cubes and it can place monkeys in the pen for you, pick slimes up and move them, and analyse them from a distance. - The [bold]mutation potion[/bold] raises a slime's mutation chance and the [bold]stabilizer potion[/bold] lowers it. A slime pushed to the maximum mutation chance becomes a [color=#ff66cc]rainbow[/color] slime when it splits.
## Temperament A fed slime is calm and only eats monkeys. A slime that [bold]starves out[/bold] with no monkey in reach turns [color=red]desperate[/color]: it feeds on any living person or animal nearby until it has eaten its fill. - Freshly split slimes start out starving. Have monkeys ready before a big split, or you will have a pen of desperate slimes about a minute later. - A desperate slime stops biting a person once they have taken about [bold]50 damage[/bold] and looks for someone else. Several hungry slimes on one person still add up fast. - Slime bites deal [bold]cellular[/bold] damage, which needs proper treatment from Medical. - [bold]Rare[/bold] and [bold]rainbow[/bold] slimes get hungry faster than common ones. - The slime scanner and the console's analyse action show each slime's mood: Calm, Hungry, [color=red]Desperate[/color] or Docile.
## Docility
Inject a [bold]pink[/bold] slime extract with [bold]plasma[/bold] to make a [bold]docility potion[/bold]. Use it on a slime to calm it for good. - A docile slime never turns desperate, even when starving. - A docile slime can be [bold]picked up and carried[/bold]. - Docility is not passed on: when a docile slime splits, its children are ordinary slimes.
## Colours and rarity Each colour can only mutate into certain others, so rare colours take several generations. - [bold]Basic:[/bold] gray - [bold]Common:[/bold] orange, purple, blue, metal - [bold]Uncommon:[/bold] yellow, dark purple, dark blue, silver, red, green, pink, gold - [bold]Rare:[/bold] bluespace, sepia, cerulean, pyrite, oil, black, light pink, adamantine - [bold]Exotic:[/bold] rainbow
## Processing - The slime processor pulls in any slime next to it that has taken at least [bold]200 damage[/bold]. Cold works well, so freeze them first. - Each slime becomes several extracts of its colour. - The processor pays [bold]research points[/bold] to the research server for every extract. Rarer colours pay much more, and the first extract of a new colour pays a large discovery bonus. - Repeats of the same colour pay less each time, so a lab earns the most by breeding new colours, not by farming one.
## Extracts
- Inject an extract with [bold]water[/bold], [bold]blood[/bold] or [bold]plasma[/bold] to set off its reaction. What happens depends on the colour and the chemical, and not every colour reacts to all three. - Reactions make materials, items, and slime potions such as steroid (more extracts per slime), extract enhancer (more uses per extract), speed, fireproofing, sentience, and docility.
## Bounties Cargo bounties sometimes ask for slime extracts by rarity. A sold extract bounty pays Federal Bills [bold]and[/bold] research points straight to the station's research server, so it is worth handing spare extracts to Cargo.
